title: Temporal integration in human auditory cortex is predominantly yoked to absolute time
goal: Reproduce the original empirical finding that integration in human auditory cortex is predominantly tied to absolute time rather than speech-structure duration, by recomputing cross-context correlations and noise ceilings from processed electrode responses across the source-defined speech-rate conditions and refitting integration-window and structure-yoking analyses with the original cohort, eligibility rules and participant/electrode hierarchy. Assess improvement on this same biological result only under an independently justified criterion; estimation-reliability comparisons remain separately named secondary evidence.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: Empirical human intracranial absolute-time versus speech-structure integration: source cross-context correlations and same-context ceilings, paired rate-specific integration windows and structure-yoking outputs, source shared-shape fitting and eligibility, and participant/electrode/stimulus hierarchy. The Fig. 3 uniform speech-rate manipulation is source-supported; final admitted condition inventory remains unresolved. Natural slow/fast speech is a separate source panel, not automatically required or covered.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.
